artworks.title: Biblis
artworks.description: Bouguereau's Academic nude: Byblis collapsed beside the spring she will become — after the letter to Caunus, the pursuit, and the tears that dissolve her into water.

artworks.title: Byblis Turning into a Spring
artworks.description: Henner paints the metamorphosis mid-flow: Byblis' body softens into the fountain that bears her name — Carian incestuous grief made liquid.

artworks.title: Biblis Changed into a Spring
artworks.description: Point's Symbolist panel: Byblis as fountain-nymph — the rejected twin whose tears become a permanent spring in Caria.

artworks.title: Biblis
artworks.description: Collin's reclining Byblis — Third Republic Ovidian nude of the sister exhausted by forbidden desire for Caunus.

artworks.title: Byblis Loves Her Brother
artworks.description: Solis' Metamorphoses woodcut: Byblis writing or pursuing Caunus — the Renaissance plate that fixed her letter and chase.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IX: Byblis' letter to her twin Caunus, the flight across Asia, and the spring born of her tears — Ovid's fullest incest metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Byblis
popCulture.description: Miletus' daughter who loved her brother Caunus and dissolved into a spring — the Carian aetiology that keeps both twins in reception.

popCulture.title: Parthenius of Nicaea
popCulture.creator: Parthenius
popCulture.description: Love Romances §11 preserves alternate Byblis endings — hanging, pursuit, and the spring — the Hellenistic dossier behind Ovid's version.
